h1: The 6 Best Small Bluetooth Trackers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Bluetooth Trackers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 small Bluetooth trackers scored on network support, battery type, sound level and form factor, from wallet cards to tag packs.
summary: The Chipolo CARD is the best small tracker for most people, because it works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub and slips into a wallet. The Tile Sticker and Tile Slim cover iPhone and Android households with a phone-finding ring. The Hauibela four-pack is the cheap way to tag a whole family's keys, and the NVQ and MSEBENT suit iPhone-only owners.
intro: The first thing to settle with a small tracker is which network it joins, because that decides whether it works at all. An Apple Find My tag is useless on an Android phone, and a Tile tag cannot use the Find My network. A tracker that quietly depends on the wrong ecosystem will tell you it is searching and find nothing.

Six small trackers made this ranking, covering wallet cards, adhesive tags and multi-packs. Each is scored on network flexibility, battery approach, sound level, size and what the listing states about range and warranty. Shapes matter as much as specs: a card fits a wallet slot that a keychain tag never will.

products.name: Chipolo CARD Rechargeable Wallet Tracker
products.verdict: A thin wallet card on Find My or Find Hub, with a 2-year warranty.
products.description:
The Chipolo CARD is a thin wallet-card tracker that joins either Apple's Find My network or Google's Find Hub. It is rechargeable, with up to a year per charge, Qi magnetic charging and a 2-year warranty. It costs $25 to $50.

The card format is the reason it wins for wallets: it fits a card slot where a thick tag will not. Rechargeable means no coin cells to replace, though the charger is not included, which is the catch. The only tracker here with a stated warranty length, it ranks ahead of the Tile pair, which cover both phone platforms but not the large Find My network.

Buy it for a wallet, passport holder or laptop sleeve. Check which network version you are ordering before checkout.

products.name: Life360 Tile Sticker Small Bluetooth Tracker
products.verdict: A small adhesive tracker for iPhone and Android with a Life360 map.
products.description:
The Tile Sticker is a small adhesive tag that works with iOS and Android, rings your phone even when it is silenced, and offers a discreet SOS alert and a Life360 family map. It costs under $25.

Adhesive is the useful detail: it sticks to a remote, a laptop or a tool where a keyring tag has nowhere to attach. Ringing your phone from the tag reverses the usual search and helps in the sofa. It ranks second because it joins the Life360 network, not Find My or Find Hub, and the listing gives no battery life or range.

Buy it for mixed iPhone and Android homes. Skip it if you want rechargeable power or a stated warranty.
products.idealFor: Mixed phone households that tag remotes and tools.
products.skipIf: You want Apple Find My network coverage.

products.name: Life360 Tile Slim Wallet Finder Bluetooth Tracker
products.verdict: Tile's thinnest tracker, made to slide into wallets and passport sleeves.
products.description:
The Tile Slim is Tile's thinnest tracker, a slide-in tag for wallets, passports and luggage, working with iOS and Android. It rings your phone even when silenced and offers a discreet SOS alert. It costs under $25.

It is the Tile answer to the Chipolo CARD, and it is cheaper. The cost of that saving is rechargeability and a stated warranty, neither of which the listing gives. It ranks just behind the Sticker because the Sticker mounts on more objects, while the Slim only suits slots and sleeves. Both share the same app and network.

Buy it for a wallet or passport at a lower price than the Chipolo. Do not expect Find My coverage.
products.idealFor: Wallets and passports on a budget.
products.skipIf: You need a rechargeable or Find My tracker.

products.name: Hauibela Smart Mini Tracker Tag 4 Pack, MFi Certified
products.verdict: Four MFi-certified Find My tags with up to 24 months of battery.
products.description:
This four-pack of mini tags works with Apple Find My and is MFi certified, with a replaceable battery rated for up to 24 months, an 80 to 100 dB speaker and Bluetooth range up to 50 meters. It costs under $25.

Four tags for that price make it the cheapest per-tag option, and the MFi certification means Apple verified the Find My integration. The 80 to 100 dB speaker is louder than the MSEBENT's 70 dB, which helps when a tag is under a cushion. It ranks fourth because it excludes Android and is a tag, not a card, so it does not fit a wallet slot.

Buy it for a family's keys, bags and bikes on iPhones. Skip it for Android phones.
products.idealFor: iPhone households tagging many items cheaply.
products.skipIf: You use Android or want a wallet card.

products.name: NVQ Key Finder, Works with Apple Find My
products.verdict: An IP67 Find My key finder with a Lost Mode and low battery alert.
products.description:
The NVQ Key Finder works with Apple Find My and is not compatible with Android. It has IP67 water resistance, rings up to 80 dB, and adds Lost Mode and a low battery alert. It costs under $25.

IP67 is rare in this price range, and it suits tags on keys, bags or a dog collar that see rain. The low battery alert is useful because tags otherwise die silently. It ranks fifth because it is a single tag at 80 dB, below the Hauibela's range, and the listing gives no battery life or size.

Buy it for outdoor use on iPhones. Skip it if you need Android support or a multi-pack.
products.idealFor: iPhone users tagging keys and bags in wet weather.

products.name: MSEBENT Air Tags 2 Pack, Apple Find My Item Finders
products.verdict: Two Find My tags with a replaceable CR2032 and sharing for up to five people.
products.description:
The MSEBENT two-pack works with Apple Find My on iOS only, measures about 1.22 x 1.22 x 0.38 inches, uses a replaceable CR2032 battery and sounds up to about 70 dB. It can be shared with up to five people. It costs under $25.

Sharing with five is the unusual spec, handy for a family tracking a car key. A CR2032 is easy to replace, though no battery life is stated. It ranks last because its 70 dB speaker is the quietest here, and the name chases an Apple product the listing does not claim to be certified against.

Buy it as a basic two-tag set for iPhone households. Skip it if volume or certification matters to you.
pros: Share with up to five people
products.idealFor: Families sharing a tracker on iPhones.
products.skipIf: You need a loud tag or Android support.

whatMatters.detail: A tracker only works on the network it is built for. Apple Find My tags need an iPhone, Tile works on iOS and Android, and Chipolo ships a Find My or Find Hub version. Confirm the network on the listing and match it to your phone before buying, because wrong choices cannot be fixed.

Rechargeable trackers like the Chipolo CARD avoid coin cells but need a charger, which is not included. Replaceable CR2032 tags are cheap to refresh. Look for a stated battery life, as the Hauibela's 24 months, and for a low-battery alert so the tag does not die silently.

A louder speaker helps when a tag sits under cushions. The Hauibela lists 80 to 100 dB, the NVQ up to 80 dB and the MSEBENT about 70 dB. Check the decibel figure on the listing, and remember sound is only useful when you are within Bluetooth range.

Wallet cards, adhesive stickers and mini tags suit different objects. A card slides into a slot, a sticker mounts on a remote and a tag clips to keys. Check the thickness in inches against your wallet slot or case, since a few millimeters can stop it fitting.

IP67 protects against dust and temporary immersion, which suits keys and bags that see rain. The NVQ lists it. A stated warranty, such as the Chipolo's two years, shows the maker expects the tag to last. Prefer listings that print one or both.

faq.a: The Tile Sticker and Tile Slim work with iOS and Android, and the Chipolo CARD has a Find Hub version. The Hauibela, NVQ and MSEBENT use Apple Find My, and the NVQ states it is not compatible with Android.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buying a tracker?
faq.a: Buying a Find My tag for an Android phone. The NVQ and MSEBENT only work with Apple's network. If you use Android, choose the Tile Sticker, Tile Slim or the Chipolo CARD Find Hub version.

faq.q: Is the Chipolo CARD worth it over the Tile Slim?
faq.a: If you want rechargeable power and a two-year warranty, yes. The CARD runs up to a year per charge and uses Find My or Find Hub. The Tile Slim costs less but lists neither.

faq.q: How do I set up a Find My tag?
faq.a: Bring the tag near your iPhone and follow the on-screen prompts, then name the item in the Find My app. The Hauibela, NVQ and MSEBENT all pair this way, and the MSEBENT can then be shared with up to five people.

faq.q: How do I replace the battery?
faq.a: The MSEBENT uses a replaceable CR2032 and the Hauibela uses a replaceable cell rated up to 24 months. Open the case, swap the cell and re-seat the cover. The Chipolo CARD recharges on a Qi magnetic charger instead.

faq.q: Will a tracker work if the item is far away?
faq.a: Bluetooth range is limited, such as the Hauibela's 50 meters in open air. Beyond that, the tag relies on the wider network, like Find My, to relay its location through nearby phones.

finalTake: The Chipolo CARD is the best small Bluetooth tracker for most people because it fits a wallet, works on Find My or Find Hub and has a rechargeable battery with a two-year warranty. The Tile Sticker and Tile Slim are the cross-platform budget choices. The Hauibela four-pack suits families with iPhones, and the NVQ and MSEBENT are narrower options.
